assumptions: The direct module caller supplies trusted tenant/item identity and an idle SQLite connection; this fixture has no caller authentication layer.
afterWrite is synchronous and only injects local faults, as specified by supplied fixture README; no async/external effect is made atomic.
Current file-backed SQLite on local filesystem is the selected environment; broader deployment/power-loss behavior is not inferred.
Invalid quantity is validated before missing item lookup; no requirement specifies precedence for simultaneously invalid/missing requests.
limitations: No automatic transaction retry. Native writer-lock error is surfaced after inherited busy timeout; explicit retry after holder rollback is verified.
Synchronous SQLite can block Node event loop, and caller-provided hooks have no execution deadline or admission bounds.
No test of process-kill/power-loss durability, disk-full, backup restore, unknown commit acknowledgement, multi-host deployment or production throughput.
Direct privileged SQL writers can bypass reserve's quantity/tenant contract; this patch preserves fixture schema and application boundary.
Two-connection forced races run on one Node event loop; actual database lock contention is separately exercised using a held transaction.
Initial verifier assertion defect is retained; final assertions use the actual stale version without implementation change.
